public_rationale: The claim is about a hypothetical: AI data centers that 'somehow succeed' with full payments and tenancy. It caps their margins at '70% at best' but does not say which margin, and it wraps that in value words ('pathetic', 'mediocre') and a hedge ('might be difficult'). Any test would need me to pick a margin type, an operator and a period he did not give. The result would turn on my choice, not on his words. For example, CoreWeave reported a 59% adjusted EBITDA margin and a negative GAAP operating margin in Q2 2026, but neither describes the successful, fully tenanted case he posits. So the claim cannot be fairly graded.
limitations: A narrower, fully specified version of the claim might be testable against project-finance data that is not public.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Even if they somehow succeed, AI data centers are pathetic businesses with mediocre margins of 70% at best, assuming consistent payments, tenancy and six years of depreciation to break even, which might be difficult because the yearly upgrade cycle makes them near-obsolete by the time they are paid off.
conditions: assuming consistent payments, tenancy, and six years of depreciation

our_interpretation: The claim describes a hypothetical: AI data centers that 'somehow succeed' with full payments and tenancy. It names no type of margin (gross, EBITDA, operating, project-level), no operator and no period.
'Pathetic' and 'mediocre' are value judgments. The obsolescence point is hedged with 'might be difficult'.
Testing it against any one operator's reported margin would mean supplying a margin type and a period he did not give. That is why earlier criteria were found unfair.
criteria.support_condition: Not testable as written. A test would need a defined margin measure for successful, fully tenanted AI data centers showing at most 70%, plus evidence that break-even takes about six years of depreciation.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not testable as written. A test would need evidence that successful, fully tenanted AI data centers reliably earn well above 70% on the measure he meant, or break even well before six years.
